messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple QTL models : Stepwiseqtl
parts:
- I've had many times where scantwo gave no results approaching significance.

- "Null QTL model" means a model with no QTLs at all. So unfortunately, there was no QTL model that had a positive penalized LOD score and so would be preferred over the model with no QTL.

karl


> On Oct 5, 2016, at 3:02 PM, Nabukalu Pheonah <nphe...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> After 'scantwo' with 1000 permutations and method="hk"
>
> H4PLscan2.perm2<-scantwo(HPL,pheno.col=8,method="hk",n.perm=1000)
>
> I start going through summaries
>
>> summary(HPLscan2.perm2,alpha = c(0.05,0.20))
> HPL (1000 permutations)
> full fv1 int add av1 one
> 5% 11.2 9.75 9.19 6.57 4.54 3.89
> 20% 10.4 9.00 8.37 5.40 3.65 2.80
>
>> summary(HPLscan2,perms =HPLscan2.perm2, alphas = c(0.2,0.2,0,0.2,0.2),pvalues = TRUE)
> There were no pairs of loci meeting the criteria.
>
>> summary(H4PLscan2,perms =H4PLscan2.perm2, alphas = c(0.5,0.5,0,0.5,0.5),pvalues = TRUE)
> There were no pairs of loci meeting the criteria.
>
> QUESTION
> I am using the "hk" method. With even adjusting the alpha threshhold as high as (0.5,0.5,0,0.5,0.5), no QTL pairs were detected. I wonder if changing to the imputation method could make a difference.
>
> Has anyone experienced this?
>
>
> I then decided to look for QTL Interactions by using this approach
>
> summary(HPLscan2,c(6.0,4.7,4.4,4.7,2.6),"best")
>
> pos1f pos2f lod.full lod.fv1 lod.int pos1a pos2a lod.add lod.av1
> c1 :c30 118 104 8.96 6.21 4.399 18 30 4.57 1.811
> c1 :c43 18 38 5.78 2.68 0.018 18 38 5.76 2.657
> c3 :c43 18 26 6.29 2.91 0.283 54 36 6.01 2.627
> c11:c30 50 104 7.29 5.50 4.536 72 44 2.75 0.963
> c11:c35 42 56 6.44 5.36 4.813 90 52 1.63 0.550
> c13:c30 138 104 7.22 5.43 4.943 110 54 2.27 0.484
> c17:c30 18 104 7.75 5.96 5.435 52 54 2.31 0.522
> c30:c30 82 104 8.66 6.87 5.166 68 74 3.49 1.703
> c30:c35 106 56 9.18 7.39 6.336 64 52 2.84 1.052
> c35:c41 56 32 9.73 7.81 6.509 52 22 3.22 1.305
> c35:c43 56 40 10.10 7.00 6.095 52 36 4.01 0.902
>
> I then used this summary to create a qtl object and model (formula=y~Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q6+Q7+Q8+Q9+Q10+Q11+Q4:Q8+Q4:Q9+Q5:Q8+Q7:Q8) to initially using in the Stepwiseqtl step in r/qtl.
>
> outsw1 <- stepwiseqtl(H4PL, pheno.col=8, max.qtl=11, penalties=pen, method="hk", verbose=FALSE)
>
> outsw1
>
> Null QTL model
>
> Question
>
> What does the "Null QTL model" above refer to? Does it mean this trait has no qtl-qtl interactions detected?
>

parts:
Hi Karl,
Yes. At a threshhold of 3 - LOD score , there was one QTL as identified in the attached summary.

Please If you have a minute look through the extract I have attached. It has some of the summary outputs from scanone, scantwo and Multiple QTL modeling (It's just a page). And it shows where the NULL QTL model is proposed. 

Another question Karl,
If you get a QTL listed as a group of markers e,g "S1_3689817~S1_3875425~S1_4247522". Do you report it this way?, Do you consider the first marker ? Or there is some way around it? I have not seen any paper where QTL markers are reported in groups. 

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple QTL models : Stepwiseqtl
parts:
The 5% significance threshold from your permutation results is ~3.89, higher than the maximum LOD score from your scanone results. That's why the stepwiseqtl results indicate no QTL.

The scanone summary will show marker names, and so I would understand "S1_3689817~S1_3875425~S1_4247522" to be the name of a single marker column in your genotype data.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple QTL models : Stepwiseqtl
parts:
Karl,

In such a case, what would be your advise on QTL interactions?
Should I just consider the scantwo two-dimensional interactions model for publication and leave out the stepwiseqtl step for forward selection and backward elimination? As a reviewer would you accept that?

Thanks
On Tue, Oct 11, 2016 at 12:13 PM, Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:

The 5% significance threshold from your permutation results is ~3.89, higher than the maximum LOD score from your scanone results. That's why the stepwiseqtl results indicate no QTL.

The scanone summary will show marker names, and so I would understand "S1_3689817~S1_3875425~S1_4247522" to be the name of a single marker column in your genotype data.

karl

parts:
From the results you present and the permutation results you got, it doesn't look like there's any very strong evidence for interactions.

So maybe focus on the two suggestive QTL from the single-QTL scan.

Generally I'd suggest saying what you did and what you found: the single-QTL analysis indicated weak evidence for a couple of loci. The two-dimensional scan and multiple-QTL analyses didn't provide any evidence for further loci, or for interactions among loci.

karl
